story.iWant: I want TypeScript type definitions for game state, events, and progression
story.soThat: So that I have type safety throughout the codebase
story.tasks: - Task 1 (AC: 1): Create `src/types/game.ts` with `GameState` interface - Task 2 (AC: 2): Create `src/types/events.ts` with `GameEvent`, `EventType`, `EventPriority` types - Task 3 (AC: 3): Create `src/types/progression.ts` with `ProgressionState` and `EquippedItems` types - Task 4 (AC: 4, 5): Review types for TypeScript best practices and architecture alignment - Task 5 (AC: 6): Verify all types are exported - Task 6 (AC: 7): Add JSDoc comments for complex types - Task 7: Testing & Validation - Verify TypeScript compilation succeeds

story-context.acceptanceCriteria:
1. **Given** the project is initialized **When** I create type definition files **Then** `src/types/game.ts` defines: `GameState` interface with properties: `coziness` (number, 0-100), `timeRemaining` (number, seconds), `score` (number, points), `activeEvents` (GameEvent[]), `isPlaying` (boolean), `isPaused` (boolean), `gameOver` (boolean)
2. **Given** the project is initialized **When** I create type definition files **Then** `src/types/events.ts` defines: `GameEvent` interface with properties: `id` (string), `type` (EventType), `priority` (EventPriority), `location` (object with x, y numbers), `timer` (number, seconds), `points` (number), `cozinessReward` (number), `cozinessPenalty` (number); `EventType` union type: `'phone' | 'kettle' | 'cat' | 'candle'`; `EventPriority` union type: `'minor' | 'standard' | 'critical'`
3. **Given** the project is initialized **When** I create type definition files **Then** `src/types/progression.ts` defines: `ProgressionState` interface with properties: `level` (number), `xp` (number), `svitlyachky` (number), `purchasedItems` (string[]), `equippedItems` (object with optional `characterSkin?`, `cat?`, `candle?` strings), `achievements` (string[])
4. **Given** type definitions are created **When** I review the type files **Then** all types follow TypeScript best practices: Use interfaces for object shapes, Use type aliases for unions/primitives, No `any` types (use `unknown` if needed), Proper generic types where applicable
5. **Given** type definitions are created **When** I compare them to the architecture document **Then** types match the architecture document data structures exactly
6. **Given** type definitions are created **When** I check the exports **Then** all types are exported for use in other modules
7. **Given** type definitions are created **When** I review complex types **Then** JSDoc comments are added for complex types

GameEvent includes: id, type, priority, location (x, y), timer (seconds), points, cozinessReward, cozinessPenalty. constraint.name: TypeScript Strict Mode

constraint.name: Type Definition Standards

constraint.name: Architecture Alignment
constraint.description: Types must match architecture document "Data Architecture" section exactly. File organization: Types organized by domain: `game.ts`, `events.ts`, `progression.ts`. All type files in `src/types/` directory. Follow architecture document "Project Structure" section.

constraint.name: Next Story Dependency
constraint.description: Story 1.3 (React Context Setup) will depend on these type definitions, so they must be complete and accurate. Types should be ready for use in Story 2.1 (Game State Management).

tests.standards: TypeScript compilation validation: Run `npm run build` or `npx tsc --noEmit` to verify no TypeScript errors. Ensure types can be imported in other files without errors. No test files exist yet (no test framework configured), but type definitions should be validated through TypeScript compiler checks.
tests.locations: Type definitions: `src/types/`. Test files (when added): Co-located with source files as `*.test.ts` or `*.spec.ts` per architecture document. Currently no test framework configured - Vitest mentioned in architecture but not yet installed.

test.description: Verify GameState interface compiles without errors and all required properties are present with correct types
Verify GameEvent, EventType, and EventPriority types compile correctly and EventType/EventPriority unions work as expected
Verify ProgressionState and EquippedItems types compile correctly with optional properties
Verify no `any` types are used (TypeScript strict mode will catch this)
Verify types match architecture document structure exactly by comparing interface definitions
Verify all types are exported by attempting imports in a temporary test file
Verify JSDoc comments are present for complex types (GameEvent, ProgressionState, EquippedItems)
